body.p: Electronic files An indexer’s use of electronic files will depend on the preferences of both the indexer and the publisher, as well as the nature of the particular job. Some indexers, and some publishers as well, still prefer to work from hardcopy proofs. Few if any professional indexers today would consider preparing an index without indexing software.

section.title: Indexing Software Capabilities
section.p: Indexing software Dedicated indexing software CINDEX MACREX SKY Index Three major dedicated indexing programs are widely used by professional indexers: CINDEX, MACREX, and SKY Index Professional. Each provides features tailored to the indexing process, including entry creation, editing, sorting, cross-reference management, and output formatting.

Embedded indexingsoftware Computer-generated indexes Embedded indexing uses software such as FrameMaker, QuarkXPress, or InDesign to insert index tags directly into the document. This approach is valuable for publications that will be reformatted or repaginated, as the index entries move with the text. However, computer- generated indexes based purely on word frequency are no substitute for human analysis.

section.title: Document Formats
section.p: PDF files Document formats Most indexers today work from PDF files, which preserve the exact appearance of the final pages. Other formats may be used depending on the project requirements.

section.title: File Transfers
section.p: File transfers Communicationelectronic files and Files are typically exchanged via email or FTP. Large files may require specialized file transfer services. Clear communication about file naming conventions and version control helps prevent confusion.
